text:
Ivy: FYI we had a customer report: a payment endpoint (POST /payments/charge) was charged twice for the same action. Repro in our tiny sample-app when the app cancels a coroutine while waiting for a network call and then retries.
Rafael: Oof. Are we sure this is a client-side retry and not server duplicate processing? Any idempotency keys?
Ivy: Server says they saw two separate requests from the client within ~500ms. The app code uses Retrofit suspend functions + our SDK Retrofit adapter. The repro is: start a payment call, rotate device to trigger config change or user nav that cancels scope, then retry. Sometimes the original request still goes out and then the retry issues a second request.
Jun: This sounds like the classic coroutine cancellation vs OkHttp Call lifecycle mismatch. When a coroutine is cancelled, the Call needs to be cancelled too; otherwise the underlying request may still run. Some Coroutine CallAdapter implementations call call.clone().enqueue(...) and cancellation wiring is delicate.
Katy: What do our SDK suspend adapters do today? I thought we wired invokeOnCancellation to call.cancel().
Ivy: We do for most cases, but our adapter uses Call.enqueue under the hood and in a tight race the clone() gets created twice (one for the original call and one for retry) and cancellation is wired to the wrong instance. Also OkHttp's Dispatcher queue + maxRequests can reorder short-lived requests which makes this flaky and platform-dependent.
Rafael: Can you paste the minimal repro snippet?
Ivy: Sure, simplified:
```
suspend fun charge(amount: Int) = api.charge(ChargeReq(amount)) // retrofit suspend
// caller
val job = lifecycleScope.launch {
  try { api.charge(100) } catch(e: Exception) { /* show error */ }
}
// user navigates away ->
job.cancel() // then user taps retry quickly
lifecycleScope.launch { api.charge(100) }
```
Jun: Two important layers: 1) retrofit's suspend adapter should cancel the same OkHttp Call when the coroutine is cancelled (and avoid double-cloning), 2) client retry policies must not retry POSTs by default.
Katy: Agreed. For the SDK I propose three changes: a) ensure suspend adapter uses a single Call instance per logical request and wiring: invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() } on the same call, b) default retryOnConnectionFailure=false for Android clients making non-idempotent methods opt-in, c) add automatic Idempotency-Key injection for charge-like endpoints or surface a helper in SDK.
Rafael: Also add a test: instrumented emulator test that cancels a coroutine mid-flight and asserts server saw at most one request per user action. That should catch regressions.
Ivy: Quick mitigation we applied in-app for the customer: add a network interceptor that injects an Idempotency-Key header and server dedupe handles duplicates. Snippet we used:
```
.addNetworkInterceptor { chain ->
  val id = UUID.randomUUID().toString()
  val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
    .header("Idempotency-Key", id)
    .build()
  chain.proceed(req)
}
```
Jun: That's good as a short-term. Longer-term we need to stop the client from issuing duplicate logical requests. The suspend adapter change is critical. Example pattern to properly wire cancellation:
```kotlin
suspend fun <T> Call.awaitSafely(): T = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { try { cancel() } catch (_: Throwable) {} }
  enqueue(object: Callback {
    override fun onResponse(call: Call, resp: Response) { cont.resume(parse(resp)) }
    override fun onFailure(call: Call, e: IOException) { cont.resumeWithException(e) }
  })
}
```
Make sure the Call that invokeOnCancellation references is the very same one used for enqueue (no accidental clone).
Katy: SDK change list for release: - retrofit adapter fix to single-call cancellation wiring; - change default OkHttp builder on Android to .retryOnConnectionFailure(false) for POSTs (or when method non-idempotent) and expose a toggle; - add optional automatic Idempotency-Key middleware; - add CI instrumented test to sample-apps. Also update docs about coroutine cancellation pitfalls and provide the awaitSafely snippet.
Rafael: One gotcha: some apps rely on retryOnConnectionFailure true for flaky mobile networks. We should provide a configurable per-endpoint retry policy and recommend idempotency keys for non-idempotent ops.
QA-Bot: reported: canary build sdk-0.14.0-rc1 started with adapter-cancel-fix branch. Integration tests scheduled: emulator API 29/31 with network churn lane.
Ivy: I'll push the repro app + server harness to internal repo and write the instrumented test. Filing follow-up issue to track docs + migration guide for mobile engineers. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
